translationRepairs: Yin rebelled against Chu, massacred Liu with Shu, raised the Jiujiang troops to welcome Qing Bu, and together marched on and massacred Chengfu, following Liu Jia as all assembled.

Zhou Yin rebelled against Chu, used troops from Shu to sack Liu, raised the forces of Jiujiang to welcome Qing Bu, and together they sacked Chengfu. They followed Liu Jia, and all the forces converged.

The preceding unit identifies 殷 as Grand Marshal Zhou Yin. Ru Chun glosses 以舒屠六 as using the troops of Shu to take or sack Liu. The accepted proposal still omitted Zhou Yin and left the final clauses ungrammatical.
Yin rebelled against Chu, massacred Liuchu with Ying Bu, raised the Jiujiang troops to welcome Ying Bu, and together marched to massacre Chengfu, following Liu Jia to all assemble.

So the feudal lords and Grand Marshal Lord Chang'an Chen Wan and 300 others, together with Erudite Ji, Successor Lord Shusun Tong, carefully chose an auspicious day, the jiawu day of the second month, and presented the honored title.

So the feudal lords and Grand Marshal, Marquis of Chang'an, Wan, and 300 others, together with the Erudite Lord Jisi, Shusun Tong, carefully chose an auspicious day, the jiawu day of the second month, and presented the honored title.
臣綰 is memorial-style Wan (not Chen Wan); 博士稷嗣君叔孫通 is Erudite Lord Jisi Shusun Tong, not “Erudite Ji, Successor Lord”.
Chen Xin, minister of the King of Jing, and ten others all said: "Grand Marshal Lu Wan, Marquis of Chang'an, has the most merit. Please establish him as King of Yan."
The King of Jing, Xin, and ten others all said: "Grand Marshal Lu Wan, Marquis of Chang'an, has the most merit. Please establish him as King of Yan."
荊王臣信 has no surname 陳, so “Chen Xin” is wrong; the proposed gloss about the memorial formula is awkward—standard X王臣Y reads as the King of Jing, Xin.
The emperor from Jinyang fought continuous battles, riding victory to pursue the enemy, reaching Loufan. Encountering great cold, soldiers with frostbitten fingers were twelve or thirteen out of ten.
The emperor from Jinyang fought continuous battles, riding victory to pursue the enemy, reaching Loufan. Encountering great cold, soldiers with frostbitten fingers were two or three in ten.
什二三 means two or three in ten, not twelve or thirteen out of ten.
On the day xinsi, he established son Ruyi as King of Dai.
On the day xinmao, he established son Ruyi as King of Dai.
辛卯 is xinmao; xinsi would be 辛巳.
On the day xinsi, he established son Ruyi as King of Dai.
On the day xinmao, he established son Ruyi as King of Dai.
辛卯 is xinmao; xinsi would be 辛巳.

Imperial Secretary Chancellor Chang reports to the prime minister, prime minister Marquis Ao reports to the feudal lords, and the imperial secretary deputy law enforcer reports to the commandery governors. Those who know men of manifest virtue must personally encourage them, prepare carriages for them, send them to the prime minister's office, and register their conduct, righteousness, and age.

The Censor-in-Chief Chang shall transmit this to the Chancellor; the Chancellor, Marquis of Zan, shall transmit it to the feudal kings; and the Palace Assistant Imperial Clerk shall transmit it to the commandery governors. Those who know men of manifest virtue must personally encourage them, prepare carriages for them, send them to the Chancellor's office, and register their conduct, righteousness, and age.
御史大夫昌下相國…相國酇侯下諸侯王…御史中執法下郡守 is a downward transmission chain; 酇侯 is Marquis of Zan, not “Marquis Ao”.
The edict said: "Marquis Nanwu Zhao Zhi is also of Yue lineage. Establish him as King of Nanhai."
The edict said: "Marquis Nanwu Zhi is also of Yue lineage. Establish him as King of Nanhai."
南武侯織 names Marquis Nanwu Zhi only; surname 趙 is not in the Chinese.

Empress Lu plotted with Shen Yiji: "The generals were formerly registered commoners together with the emperor; they faced north and became subjects, but their hearts have always been resentful. Now they are to serve a young ruler. Unless their clans are exterminated, the world will not be at peace."

Empress Lü plotted with Shen Yiji: "The generals were formerly registered commoners together with the emperor; they faced north and became subjects, but their hearts have always been resentful. Now they are to serve a young ruler. Unless their clans are exterminated, the world will not be at peace."
呂后 is Empress Lü; plain “Lu” conflates 呂 with 盧 (as in Lu Wan) in this chapter.
Someone heard and told Ji Shang.
Someone heard and told Li Shang.
酈商 is Li Shang; “Ji Shang” misreads 酈.
Ji Shang saw Shen Shiqi and said: "Heard the emperor has passed away. Four days without announcing death, wanting to execute the generals.
Li Shang saw Shen Shiqi and said: "Heard the emperor has passed away. Four days without announcing death, wanting to execute the generals.
酈商 is Li Shang; “Ji Shang” is the same misreading as in the preceding unit.
